chunks.arabic_text: وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ:

translations.en: And it was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ الرَّجُلُ يَخْرُجُ فِي تِجَارَةٍ إِلَى مَكَّةَ أَوْ يَكُونُ لَهُ إِبِلٌ فَيُكْرِيهَا حَجَّتُهُ نَاقِصَةٌ أَوْ تَامَّةٌ

translations.en: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A man goes out in trade to Makkah, or he has camels and rents them out. Is his hajj incomplete or complete?"
He عليه السلام said: "No; rather, his hajj is complete."

en.summary: This hadith states that if a person performs hajj while also engaging in trade or renting out camels, that does not diminish the validity or completeness of his hajj. It indicates that lawful economic activity accompanying the pilgrimage does not make the hajj deficient.
en.seo_question: Is hajj still complete if someone travels for trade or rents out camels during it?

key_terms.تِجَارَةٍ: trade or commercial activity undertaken during travel
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the destination of the pilgrimage journey
key_terms.إِبِلٌ: camels owned for transport or rental use
key_terms.فَيُكْرِيهَا: then he rents them out for use
key_terms.حَجَّتُهُ: his hajj, meaning his pilgrimage act
key_terms.نَاقِصَةٌ: deficient or incomplete in reward or validity
